1.title: A Frog on a Log
1.topic: a frog on a log on a hot day catches a bug and jumps into the pond (animals, nature)
lines: A *big* *frog* | *sits* on a *log*. ↘
The *sun* is *hot*. | The frog says, | “*Ribbit*!”
A *bug* *zips* past. | The *frog* can *see* it.
*Zap*! | He *gets* the *bug*. | *Yum*, | *yum*! ↘
Then *hop*, | *hop*, | *splash*! | He is *in* the *pond*.
Is the *frog* *hot*? ↗ | *Not* *now*! ↘
sounds: 입을 동그랗고 크게 벌려 '아'에 가깝게 짧게: hot '핫', log '라그'.
u는 힘을 빼고 짧게 '어': sun '썬', bug '버그'.
f-r, s-p-l을 '으' 없이 붙여서 한 번에: frog는 '프로그'가 아니라 'fr-og'.
1.expression: Sound lazy and sleepy on the first line, use a deep frog voice for “Ribbit!”, say “Zap!” fast and sharp, make “splash” big and loud, ask the question with your voice going up, then answer “Not now!” with a happy grin.

2.title: Bunny Ears
2.topic: a boy learns to tie his shoes with Grandma's bunny-ears trick (family, perseverance, feelings)
lines: Theo *wanted* to tie | his *own* shoes.
He *crossed* the laces | and *pulled* them *tight*.
He *looped* one lace. | It *slipped*! | Theo *sighed*.
“Try *bunny ears*!” | Grandma *showed* him *how*.
He *made* two *loops* | and *tucked* one *under*.
He *pulled* them | *slowly*. | Did it *work*? ↗
“I *did* it!” | Theo *shouted*. | Grandma *clapped*.
The next *day*, | Theo *tied* his shoes | by *himself*! ↘
sounds: s, p, k 뒤의 -ed는 짧은 t: looped '룹트', tucked '턱트'.
끝을 올려요. work를 살짝 높게, 두근두근하는 목소리로.
2.expression: Sound eager at first, drop your voice with a big sigh on “Theo sighed,” use a kind Grandma voice, hold your breath on “Did it work?”, then shout “I did it!” and end proudly.

3.title: Questions for Grandpa
3.topic: a child interviews her grandpa, a Navy veteran, for a Veterans Day class project (community, family, holidays)
lines: On *November* eleventh, | America *celebrates* | *Veterans* Day.
*Veterans* are people | who *served* in the *military* | to *protect* our *country*.
This year, | my teacher asked us | to *interview* a *veteran*.
I *called* my *grandpa*. | He was in the *Navy* | for *twenty* years.
“*Where* did you *live*?” ↘ | I asked *first*. | “On a huge *ship*,” | he said. | “It was like a *floating* city.”
“Were you ever *scared*?” ↗ | Grandpa was *quiet* | for a *moment*.
“*Sometimes*,” | he said. | “But my *friends* on the ship | helped me be *brave*.”
“What did you *miss* the most?” ↘ | He *laughed*. | “Grandma's *cooking*!”
On Veterans Day, | I *read* my interview | to the whole *class*.
Grandpa *came* to *listen*, | wearing his *Navy* cap.
At the *end*, | everyone *stood* up | and said, | “*Thank* you | for your *service*!” ↘
sounds: “Where did you live?” ↘ / “Were you ever scared?” ↗
Where, What으로 시작하는 질문은 끝을 내리고, Were/Did로 시작하는 질문은 끝을 올려요.
긴 단어는 힘주는 음절 하나만 크고 길게, 나머지는 가볍게. protect는 뒤에 힘!
자음 끝 + 모음 시작은 이어서: stood up → '스투덥'. Thank you → '땡큐'처럼 한 덩어리로.
3.expression: Read it like a young reporter: clear and steady for the facts about Veterans Day, curious when you ask each question, slower and deeper for Grandpa's answers, a warm laugh on “Grandma's cooking!”, and a proud, loud “Thank you for your service!” at the end.

4.title: The Amazing Octopus
4.topic: how an octopus squeezes, changes color, squirts ink and solves puzzles (animals, ocean, science)
lines: Deep in the *ocean*, | a rock *seems* to *move*. | Look *closer*. | It's not a rock at *all*. | It's an *octopus*!
An octopus has *eight* long *arms* | and *no* *bones* in its body.
Because it has no bones, | it can *squeeze* through a *crack* | much *smaller* than its body.
Each arm is covered with *suckers*. | They help the octopus *grab*, ↗ | *taste*, ↗ | and *feel* things. ↘
The octopus is also | a *master* of *disguise*.
Special cells in its *skin* | can change *color* | in less than a *second*.
It can even make its skin *bumpy* | to look like *rocks* | or *seaweed*.
If a *hungry* shark finds it anyway, | the octopus has *another* trick.
It shoots out a cloud of dark *ink* | and *zooms* away | while the shark is *confused*.
Here's a *surprising* fact: | an octopus has *three* hearts, | and its blood is *blue*!
Scientists also say | that octopuses are very *smart*.
In *aquariums*, | some have learned to *open* jars | to get the *food* inside.
A *few* have even *escaped* from their tanks | at *night*!
So the next time you see a *rock* in the ocean, | look *twice*. | It might be *looking* back at *you*! ↘
sounds: 힘주는 음절을 크고 길게. octopus는 앞에, disguise·confused는 뒤에 힘을 줘요.
여러 개를 나열할 때 앞의 것은 살짝 올리고, 마지막 것만 내려요.
혀끝을 윗니 아래에 살짝 대고 바람을 내보내요. three는 '쓰리'가 아니라 'θree'.
4.expression: Read it like a nature documentary narrator: soft and mysterious at the start, then “It's an octopus!” with a surprise, amazed and clear for each fact, quick and sneaky on “zooms away,” extra excited on the three hearts and blue blood, and playful and spooky on the last line.
practice: It might be looking back at you!
